scope: Proposition 8.3 (Weak local maps) of the manuscript “BKT universality for height and planar spin fields” (preprints/BKT-universality-for-height-and-planar-spin-fields-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 216 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 5e6a8df09e021c4a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 127. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Choose the regulator parameters and h0 first, then L sufficiently large, and then A sufficiently large depending on L. On a fixed small activity ball the exact partition algebra induces analytic maps    t+ z+ R+    =    t + Pt j R λjz + Pz j R CjR    + Nj(t, z, R), ∥Cj∥ ≤ θ < 1, ∥Pt j ∥ + ∥Pz j ∥ ≤ CL,A, (8.15) where θ can be chosen arbitrarily small and ∥Nj(t, z, R)∥ ≤ CL,A(|t| + |z| + ∥R∥)2 . (8.16) The same ball has uniform analytic Taylor coefficient and differentiated estimates at fixed a′. These assertions hold on a fixed one-sided reference interval k0 ≤ a′ ≤ k0 + δref, uniformly in sufficiently spread-out Jρ for the first kernel family. For every fixed J, they hold at a sufficiently large starting scale for either the first family or the entry family of Lemma 8.1. On a compact subinterval of a′ > k0, one may omit the cosine coordinate and leave every charged activity in the remainder. Choose L depending on the gap from k0; then the corresponding map has the same assertions with its z row deleted. For a′ ≥ 4k0 there is also such a map with a charged contraction uniform in a′. The scalar coefficients obtained on the plane are exactly the torus coefficients through the stopping scale. Torus remainders and their activity derivatives obey the same estimates. Each fixed-support finite recursion and each finite scalar projection is continuous in the parameters while its preceding activities remain in the small ball. This last assertion does not assert norm analyticity under variation of α.
